title: Orca Retail - Pricing fit & hosting options discovery
summary: Intro + qualification: Orca wants to add LLM features to product search and chat. Main constraints: tight latency SLOs for web UX, strict budget (~$25k/mo) for inference, and regulatory requirement for audit logs and KMS. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, batching/caching levers, and a scoped pilot to validate unit economics and latency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pilot pricing, security pack, and a simple benchmark plan; customer to share sample traffic profile and decision stakeholders.

Priya Rao: Confirm compliance contacts and internal SSO/KMS details (due 2026-03-10)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 16:00 PST
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Liam (Head of ML - Orca), Priya (Platform Eng - Orca), Carlos (CTO - Orca)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Orca is exploring options to power search-rewrite and conversational help with LLMs. They're cost sensitive, have low-latency UX needs, and some compliance requirements for logs and key management. They want a pilot to validate per-token economics and latency on both hosted and dedicated footprints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Jonas is our solutions engineer. Quick round of intros?
[00:08] Liam: Hey, Liam here, lead ML at Orca. Priya's joining from platform, Carlos is on if we need CTO level decisions.
[00:15] Priya: Hi all.
[00:17] Jonas: Hi, good to meet you. Quick agenda — understand your workloads, constraints, then walk hosting options and levers like batching and KV cache, and close with pilot next steps. Sound okay?
[00:27] Carlos: Yep, good.

[00:32] Liam: To kick off, high level — we want to augment product search with generative re-ranks and a chat assistant for support. Latency expectations on search path are pretty strict — ideally 150-250ms tail for the user-facing completions, and budget is, uh, roughly $20-30k a month for inference initially. We can trade some latency for cost but UX matters.
[00:54] Maya: Helpful. When you say completions, what's avg token count and qps?
[00:58] Liam: Average prompt is ~100 tokens, completion ~40–60 tokens. Peak qps for search enrichment is around 60 qps but bursty; steady-state maybe 15–20. Monthly calls ballpark 3 million requests, maybe 300–400 million tokens/month depending on prompt length.
[01:17] Priya: We also have data residency concerns — some logs must stay in our VPC for a subset of requests, and we need audit logs and KMS integration for encryption at rest. SOC 2 is a requirement for our procurement.
[01:29] Jonas: Totally understandable. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys in our Private offering; Dedicated can also be configured to only talk to your KMS depending on network. Hosted can support bring-your-own-key for certain tiers, but there are tradeoffs.
[01:42] Carlos: Can you explain the cost levers — per-token pricing vs batching and cache? We need to model things so finance signs off.
[01:50] Maya: Sure. At a high level we bill per token for hosted usage. For Dedicated you have reserved GPU capacity which gives you a predictable monthly cost and lower per-token compute costs because you control the instance pool. The two big levers to reduce per-token cost without sacrificing quality: batching (pack multiple requests into a single forward pass) and KV/prefix caching for repeated context.
[02:12] Liam: How much can batching help for our bursty qps? We're worried about increased latency for individual requests.
[02:18] Jonas: Good question. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching: it will batch small windows of time (tens of ms) to increase throughput. You can tune the batching latency SLO — if you set a 50ms batching window you'll get better amortization but slightly higher p99 latency. For tail-sensitive paths like search we often recommend a small batching window + a lower-latency tier or a cheap baseline fallback model for cold calls.
[02:41] Priya: And the KV cache — is that per customer? How does it handle privacy?
[02:44] Jonas: KV cache is per-customer and can be encrypted with your KMS. It's best for repeated prefixes or session-based chat — it avoids re-computing the prefix attention which saves tokens and compute time. One gotcha: it helps more when prompts share prefixes; for very diverse prompts, less benefit. Also we can evict or zero-out cache for queries considered PII.
[03:05] Liam: Ok. On numbers — if we run a hosted pilot, what's the expected per-token price ballpark and how does that change if we move to dedicated?
[03:12] Maya: Hosted per-token varies by model family; rough publicly available ballpark: $0.0008–$0.004 per token depending on model size and context. For a realistic model we might be in the mid-range, say $0.0012/token for a 70B variant. Dedicated reserved capacity could reduce compute cost materially — maybe a 30–60% reduction in compute per-token depending on utilization and quantization. But then you pay reserved instance costs. We'll model that in the pricing spreadsheet.
[03:38] Carlos: So if our 3M requests x ~160 tokens average (prompt+completion) we get ~480M tokens. At $0.0012 that's ~576k a month, which is way over our budget. So clearly we need batching and smaller models or quantized variants.
[03:52] Jonas: Exactly — three knobs: pick a smaller but tuned model (e.g., 13B or 30B quantized), use batching, and apply prefix caching. Also consider hybrid routing: high-SLA queries go to a higher-cost model/route, lower priority queries go to a cheaper model. That reduces overall unit cost while protecting UX.
[04:12] Liam: Can Redwood route by policy? Like by route, user tier, or latency requirement?
[04:16] Maya: Yes, smart routing is built-in — you can define policies by route, token budget, or SLA. We also support automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity is constrained.
[04:25] Priya: For procurement, we need SOC 2 report, data flow diagrams, and a list of subcontractors. Can you provide those?
[04:31] Maya: Yes — we'll send the security pack. We also have whitepapers on VPC/private deployments and a guide for KMS integration.
[04:38] Carlos: If we went Dedicated, what's the process and timeline? We have a Q2 goal to start pilot; ideally a dedicated reserved pool by Q3 if pilot looks good.
[04:46] Jonas: Dedicated setup is relatively fast for reserved pools — after contract it's usually 2–4 weeks to provision, but the pilot can start immediately on hosted or a small dedicated sandbox depending on procurement. For Private (VPC), there's more setup for networking—usually 4–8 weeks depending on approvals.
[05:03] Liam: We're also comparing Anthropic / Bedrock for pricing — they have different per-token and model choices. What are Redwood's differentiators for unit economics?
[05:11] Maya: A few things — our runtime has aggressive batching and KV cache optimizations, model variant recommendations tied to your workload, and a unified toolchain so you can run the same workload across hosted, dedicated, and private. We focus on observable unit economics (token-level breakdowns) so teams can iterate on prompts and routing to hit budget targets.
[05:29] Priya: Any notable hidden costs we should consider? Storage of logs? Long-term K-V storage?
[05:33] Jonas: Logging retention beyond the default window, additional retention for audit logs, or options for extended observability incur add-on charges. Also data egress for private deployments may have network charges depending on your cloud. We'll call those out in the pricing doc.
[05:46] Carlos: For the pilot we want to see two things: 1) realistic latency numbers at p50/p95/p99 for our traffic profile; 2) an accurate cost model so finance can see run-rate.
[05:56] Maya: Perfect. Proposed pilot: 72-hour benchmark covering three profiles — baseline (steady 20 qps), peak bursts (simulate your weekend peak 60 qps), and mixed chat (session affinity to test KV cache). We'll run hosted + a dedicated small pool and report latency and cost per bucket. Jonas will own the perf plan.
[06:15] Liam: Works for us. We'll share example prompts and a 7-day traffic histogram. Is there anything else we should instrument?
[06:21] Jonas: If you can share a sample of prompt distributions and a few blackbox metrics (client-side latencies), we'll instrument end-to-end. Also, tokenization differences matter — we'll include recommended tokenization checks.
[06:33] Priya: About encryption: you said hosted supports BYOK for some tiers. Our security team may require a full private control plane.
[06:39] Maya: Noted — we'll include a matrix showing what security controls are available in hosted vs dedicated vs private. For BYOK and complete tenant isolation, Private/VPC is the safest path.
[06:49] Carlos: On SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM + SAML + audit trails available to integrate with our IAM.
[06:55] Jonas: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise tiers. Audit events can be shipped to your SIEM and we support fine-grained RBAC in console.
[07:04] Liam: Quick question — does Redwood support model quantization and can you give guidance on accuracy tradeoffs?
[07:09] Jonas: Yes — we onboard quantized variants and provide recommendations per workload. Typical tradeoffs: 4-bit quantization can introduce some generation quality drift for instruction-following, but for retrieval-augmented search re-ranking it's usually negligible. We'll run quality evals during the pilot to validate.
[07:26] Maya: Ok, recapping next steps — Redwood: send pilot pricing and security pack, Jonas to share benchmark plan, Orca to share traffic and prompt samples, schedule kickoff. Any other ask?
[07:37] Priya: Can you also include a sample SLA and uptime numbers for Dedicated? Procurement will want that.
[07:42] Maya: We'll include SLA and sample contract terms for Dedicated and Private tiers.
[07:46] Carlos: Great. Thanks everyone.
[07:49] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD with the docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription accuracy: occasional proper names may be misrecognized (e.g., "K-V cache" vs "KV cache"). Speaker labels are as recorded; partial overlaps and filler words removed in a few places.
questions: What is typical per-token price for the recommended model?
How quickly can Dedicated be provisioned after contract?
Can KMS be customer-managed in hosted or only in private?
